skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray showing complete opacification (white-out) of a hemithorax to determine the underlying etiology based on mediastinal position.
steps: Assess the direction of the mediastinal shift (trachea and heart) relative to the side of the opacity.
If the mediastinum is shifted toward the opaque side, diagnose volume loss causes such as total lung atelectasis or fibrosis.
If the mediastinum is shifted away from the opaque side (contralateral shift), diagnose space-occupying processes such as massive pleural effusion, pyopneumothorax, or large mass.
If the mediastinum remains central despite complete opacification, consider causes with balanced forces like pneumonia combined with effusion or fixed mediastinum.
